answer: The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 32% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the adversary's own capital. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the prism reward in the tundra ledger costs the operator directly, and the violet audit records each payout. A farm of 295 keys as a result funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
